answer: ACCEPT. This is the kind of PR Linus likes: 332 additions, 949 deletions, net -617. Two whole crates die (kernel + app, ~700 lines), plus an obsolete archive payload, plus three catalog yamls, plus a stale Cargo.lock and workspace member list. The lane never had a sustainable invariant — it was one-time pre-grit cutover hygiene masquerading as reusable CI. Killing it is correct. The pr-review-dispatcher Cargo.toml change is a 4-line collateral edit (likely a dep removed), not a bundled new app — meta confirms +2/-2. Scope is clean: one lane, one ADR, one retirement event.
key_claims: Net deletion of ~617 lines (332 add / 949 del) across 24 files — deletion-first as Linus prefers.
Kernel + app + 3 catalog yamls + workspace members + Cargo.lock entries all removed together — no half-retirement leaving dead symbols.
ADR-0118 is 66 lines, not 100+ — context/decision/consequences/rejected-alternatives, no padding. Acceptable ceremony for a lane retirement that supersedes ADR-0052.
Pre-grit archive payload (`bominal/.../pre-grit-cutover-2026-05-12/README.md`) deleted; the lane that policed it dies with it. Symmetric.

Amendments to ADR-0104/0107 are one-line edits redirecting readers — not rewrites. ADR-0104 swaps a 'candidate extension' line for the actual landed crate name. ADR-0107 changes the table row from RENAME to RETIRED. This is the minimum viable forward-reference, not ceremony.
Lane retirement is justified in-text: ADR-0116 made M-CC-P11 the canonical VCS substrate; an always-empty runner would be 'false mechanical confidence' (their words, which Linus would endorse).
uncertainty_areas: The dispatcher app dep edit was not fully visible in the diff tail (truncated at line 518) — relying on PR meta showing +2/-2.
Cannot independently confirm the lane was never wired into a green CI run that other code depended on — but the retirement IP-008 doc shows it was a P6/P7 one-time gate, not a recurring CI lane.

anti_patterns_detected.pattern: minor: lane doc files kept as tombstones instead of deleted outright
anti_patterns_detected.note: Both `.omc/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md` and `docs/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md` survive as 12-line retirement stubs. Linus would prefer deleting them and recording the lane death in ADR-0118 + CHANGELOG only. But traceability for IP-008 evidence is a reasonable defense, and the stubs are small.

anti_patterns_detected.pattern: minor: doctrine spec files (decision-principles.json, forbidden-operations.json, masterplan.json, crate-naming-audit.json) get +191/-77 of edits in a 'retire one lane' PR
anti_patterns_detected.note: Bundles doctrine drift into a cleanup PR. Probably necessary to keep machine-readable specs honest, but increases blast radius vs a pure deletion PR. Acceptable because the edits are direct consequences of the retirement.

findings.summary: Two tombstone lane docs (`.omc/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md`, `docs/fitness-lanes/archive-orphan.md`) survive as 12-18-line retirement stubs when ADR-0118 + INDEX.md + CHANGELOG already carry the historical record.
findings.recommended_action: Optional follow-up: delete the two stub files and rely on the INDEX retirement row + ADR-0118 for IP-008 traceability. Not a blocker — current state is consistent.

findings.summary: ADR-0118 'Verification plan' lists steps already executed in PR validation — duplicates the PR body instead of pointing to it.
findings.recommended_action: Optional: collapse the ADR verification plan to one line referencing the PR validation block. Not blocking.
